description: DRAFT industry rubric pack APPAREL_TEXTILE: HIRA calibration v2 evaluation fixtures for an Indian garment / textile unit. 5 activities: 2 low-hazard (APP-01, APP-02) and 3 high-hazard (APP-03..APP-05). Same structure as tests/eval/hira_calibration/activities.json: for DRAFT activities the per-hazard likelihood/severity are what an uncalibrated LLM (the v1 Copilot) proposed, often over-stated; recommendedControls are the controls it proposed. Hazards are seeds for the HSE lead to validate. 'expected' is an HSE judgement still to be made ('TODO(HSE lead)'); it must not be fitted to engine output.

STD_5X5.note: Standard 5x5, frequency-anchored likelihood, MODERATE tolerable with ALARP.

JSL_QSD24_GT.note: JSL Hisar plant method QSD/24 (GT > 3.33 significant): plant-index likelihood, MODERATE not acceptable.

activities.title: Sewing on single-needle lockstitch machines
activities.activity: Stitching shirt panels on single-needle lockstitch machines on the sewing line (piece-rate operators, 9-10 hour shifts)

hazards.name: Needle puncture at the presser foot
hazards.consequence: Operator's finger slips under the descending needle while guiding a small panel at the presser foot: needle pierces the fingertip or nail, sometimes leaving a broken needle tip in the finger

hazards.name: Needle breakage
hazards.consequence: Needle snaps on a thick seam or a button and the fragment flies towards the operator's eye: eye injury

hazards.name: Sustained sitting at the machine
hazards.consequence: Operators sit 9-10 hours on fixed-height stools without backrests, bent over the machine bed: chronic neck, shoulder and lower-back pain

hazards.name: Repetitive sewing operations
hazards.consequence: Repetitive pinching, guiding and thread trimming at about 1,200 operations an hour: wrist tendinitis or carpal tunnel syndrome developing over months

existingControls.description: Finger (needle) guard fitted on every single-needle lockstitch machine
existingControls.verificationMethod: Line-start machine checklist signed by the line supervisor each shift

existingControls.description: Transparent eye guard fitted at the needle bar on all machines
Broken-needle policy: every fragment recovered, matched and logged before work resumes
existingControls.verificationMethod: Needle register checked by the QA in-charge every shift

existingControls.description: Height-adjustable chairs with backrests on 4 of the 10 sewing lines
Two 10-minute stretching breaks per shift, led by the line supervisor

recommendedControls.description: Needle guard on all machines
Ergonomic chairs with backrest and footrest for all operators
Job rotation between sewing operations
Training
Finger guards / thimbles for operators
Servo motors with needle positioning on all machines

activities.title: Steam ironing and garment finishing
activities.activity: Pressing finished garments with steam-electric irons on vacuum ironing tables in the finishing hall, steam supplied from the central boiler

hazards.name: Steam leak from the iron hose
hazards.consequence: Steam escapes from a cracked iron hose or a loose hose clamp onto the presser's hand and forearm: scald, usually superficial

hazards.name: Hot iron sole plate
hazards.consequence: Presser's free hand or forearm touches the 150-180 C sole plate while smoothing the garment: contact burn (blister)

hazards.name: Damaged iron cord
hazards.consequence: Presser gets a shock from a frayed iron cord or an un-earthed iron body while touching the metal vacuum table on a floor wet with steam condensate

hazards.name: Hot finishing hall in summer
hazards.consequence: Pressers stand 9 hours beside steam irons in a hall at 36-38 C in May-June: dehydration and heat exhaustion

hazards.name: Standing all shift at the ironing table
hazards.consequence: Standing all shift at a fixed-height ironing table: leg swelling and lower-back pain

existingControls.description: Thermostat-controlled steam irons with silicone heat-resistant iron rests
Monthly check of iron cords, plugs and steam hoses by the maintenance electrician
Exhaust fans and evaporative air coolers in the finishing hall
Cotton glove on the non-ironing hand

recommendedControls.description: Steel-braided steam hoses with crimped fittings
30 mA RCCB on the ironing table power circuits
Heat stress awareness, ORS and drinking water at the finishing line
Anti-fatigue mats at the ironing tables
Training

activities.title: Straight-knife and band-knife cutting of fabric lays
activities.activity: Cutting 60-80 ply fabric lays with a straight-knife cutting machine and cutting small blocks to shape on the band-knife machine in the cutting room

hazards.name: Straight-knife blade contact
hazards.consequence: Cutter's free hand, pressing down the lay in front of the machine, meets the reciprocating straight-knife blade: deep laceration, cut tendons or a severed fingertip

hazards.name: Band-knife blade contact
hazards.consequence: Operator's fingers follow a small fabric block into the running band-knife blade at the table slot: finger amputation

hazards.name: Band-knife blade breakage
hazards.consequence: Band-knife blade snaps and whips out of the wheel housing: laceration to the operator's face or arm

hazards.name: Trailing straight-knife cable
hazards.consequence: Straight-knife power cable dragged across the table is nicked by the blade and the cutter grips the bare conductor: electric shock

hazards.name: Bending over the cutting table
hazards.consequence: Cutters bend over a 90 cm table and push the straight knife through thick lays all shift: lower-back and shoulder strain

existingControls.description: Stainless-steel chain-mail glove on the non-cutting hand for every straight-knife and band-knife cutter
existingControls.verificationMethod: Glove issue register; cutting master checks at shift start

existingControls.description: Straight knives with an adjustable blade guard lowered to the lay height
Band knife with enclosed upper and lower wheel guards, adjustable blade guard set just above the work, and push sticks for small pieces
existingControls.verificationMethod: Weekly machine guard checklist by maintenance

existingControls.description: Straight-knife cables run from an overhead festoon rail above the cutting table
Only trained and authorised cutters operate the knives (authorisation list on the cutting room board)

recommendedControls.description: Chain-mail gloves for all cutters
Blade guards on all cutting machines
Training of cutters
Anti-fatigue mats and height-adjustable cutting tables
Automatic CNC fabric cutter for long runs
Daily inspection of band-knife blades for cracks

items: IR-2026-019: straight-knife cut to a cutter's left index finger at table 3 (4 stitches, no lost time)
FA-2025-144: straight-knife nick to the thumb while squaring a lay (first aid)

activities.title: Unloading and stacking of fabric rolls and bales
activities.activity: Manual unloading of fabric rolls (40-70 kg) and compressed fabric / yarn bales from trucks and stacking them on the fabric store floor and racks

hazards.name: Carrying rolls and bales
hazards.consequence: Loaders carry 40-70 kg fabric rolls and bales on their shoulders from the truck to the store: lower-back injury (disc prolapse) or shoulder strain

hazards.name: Rolls falling from floor stacks
hazards.consequence: A fabric roll from the top of a 6-high floor stack rolls off and strikes a loader's head or crushes a foot

hazards.name: Fall from the truck bed
hazards.consequence: Loader steps backwards off the 1.4 m truck bed edge while pulling a bale: fall onto the yard, fracture or head injury

hazards.name: Truck reversing to the store shutter
hazards.consequence: Truck reverses to the store shutter without a banksman and pins a loader against the plinth: crush injury, possible fatality

hazards.name: Cotton fibre dust
hazards.consequence: Loaders breathe cotton fibre dust when bale wrapping tears: respiratory irritation; byssinosis after years of exposure

existingControls.description: Safety shoes and cotton gloves for loaders

recommendedControls.description: Hand pallet truck and roll trolleys for moving rolls
Roll racks with end stops; floor stacks limited to 4 high and chocked
Banksman for reversing trucks
Manual handling training
Dust mask
Mobile loading ramp at the store dock

activities.notes: Only baseline PPE recorded: loading crew supplied by a labour contractor.

activities.title: Air-jet loom weaving and lint cleaning
activities.activity: Running 120 air-jet looms, mending warp / weft breaks and blow-cleaning lint from the looms with compressed air in the humidified weaving shed

hazards.name: Weaving shed noise
hazards.consequence: Weavers spend 12-hour shifts in 98-102 dB(A) air-jet loom noise: permanent noise-induced hearing loss

hazards.name: Lint and fabric fire
hazards.consequence: Lint layered on loom motors, light fittings and humidification ducts is ignited by an overheated motor bearing or an electrical spark and the fire flashes across the lint through the shed: burns to weavers, possible multiple casualties during evacuation

hazards.name: Reed / sley beat-up
hazards.consequence: Weaver's fingers caught between the beating reed and the cloth fell while mending a broken end without stopping the loom: crushed or fractured fingers

hazards.name: Compressed-air blow cleaning
hazards.consequence: Lint, broken filament and grit blown off the loom at 6 bar strike the weaver's eye: eye injury

hazards.name: Hot humid weaving shed
hazards.consequence: Shed kept at 75-85% RH and 34-36 C in summer: heat exhaustion of weavers on 12-hour shifts

recommendedControls.description: Ear plugs or ear muffs for all weavers
Shift-wise lint cleaning with vacuum instead of compressed air
Automatic fire detection and sprinklers in the weaving shed
Stop the loom before mending breaks
Training
Safety goggles during blow cleaning

existingControlProposals.description: Lint cleaning schedule: looms, motors and overhead fittings vacuum-cleaned every shift, humidification ducts weekly
existingControlProposals.verificationMethod: Shift cleaning checklist signed by the jobber

existingControlProposals.description: Ear plugs (SNR 25) issued to all weavers, replaced monthly

activities.notes: No controls captured in the draft (weaving shed added from scratch); the plant registers hold two.
